title: Applying Half-Frame Photography
slide_intent: Change the image-text arrangement with the format because the same hierarchy must survive a vertical composition.
strategic_value: The two stacked examples can extend Burger King’s photographic layout system without changing its headline and signature relationships.
demonstration: Two vertical examples place burger photographs above cream typography panels; one has a large headline, and the other accommodates smaller text and body copy.
practical_value: Move the photograph above the type panel while retaining the preceding page’s spacing rules.

content_islands.name: Orientation guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the short note at left; it calls the upper image full-frame while the title remains Half-Frame Photography.

content_islands.name: Large-headline example
content_islands.spec: Place the burger close-up above the larger headline and small subhead.

content_islands.name: Detailed example
content_islands.spec: Place the hands-and-burger photograph above a smaller headline, subhead and body line.

ingredient.name: Stacked photo and type
ingredient.role: Adapt the image-text relationship to a vertical format.
ingredient.application: Place the photographic panel above typography and retain the separation rules from page 87.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2020 partner guidelines, PDF produced January 2021. The body says full-frame photography, but the displayed applications retain a separate type panel; do not interpret it as a full-background overlay.

reference_purposes.Application: Two vertical layouts show photography above the text rather than beside it.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The text explicitly carries forward the previous page’s rules.
